priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock. This is a real, mapped, qualification-locked mechanism (Tier 4 Final aftertreatment on CAT's own large reciprocating-engine platforms, exactly what a minor-NSR permit's BACT presumption forces onto the engine) sitting inside a company posting record quarterly revenue on genuinely accelerating data-center-driven Power Generation demand (filing_evidence[0], [2]), and a raised FY2026 guide to mid-to-high-teens total revenue growth (WebSearch 2026-08-04, CNBC/Seeking Alpha, not filing-verified). But the trailing multiple has done almost all of the work over the past year, not earnings: on the last annual EPS available at each point in time, CAT's trailing P/E went from about 18.5x near the 2025-09-09 low (418.09, priced against FY2024 EPS 22.57) to a peak near 55.8x at the 2026-06-30 high (1,064.90, priced against FY2025 EPS 19.09, itself DOWN 15.4% from FY2024 on a $1.3-1.5 billion tariff hit) and sits at about 42.6x today. The market-implied five-year FCF CAGR (28.57%) exceeds even this dive's own stretch case (17.54%, a 12% revenue CAGR at a 21% margin near CAT's pre-tariff peak) by 10.93 points, a real gap that survives the file's own horizon-sensitivity test at 5 years but NOT at 10 years, where the same market ask falls to 16.23% and sits only 4.11 points above this dive's 12.12% base case, inside the file's own 12.34-point horizon_spread. Layered on top: no filing on disk attributes any dollar figure to the aftertreatment content specifically (it is a sub-component of Power Generation, itself roughly 40% of Power & Energy segment sales, itself part of a $67.6 billion company), Cummins is promoted to O1 on this identical link this same run (duplicate_exposure), CAT is one of the most heavily analyst-covered and institutionally owned names on this desk's slate (28 analysts, 71% institutional, WebSearch 2026-09-06), and a real, disclosed, litigation-linked $392 million 'expected' tariff-recovery item sits inside the very quarter the bull case leans on for margin recovery. Not TOO_LATE: the priced-in decomposition here is genuinely ambiguous rather than conclusive, since a true trailing-twelve-month EPS cannot be built from the fundamentals on disk (only FY totals plus two quarters' EPS are available, data_gaps), and the most recent quarterly print shows real earnings acceleration (EPS +68.2% year over year) that a pure annual-EPS comparison does not capture; calling TOO_LATE off an incomplete decomposition would be exactly the defect method section 1 exists to prevent. Not INVESTABLE: no margin of safety exists at today's price on the tougher of the two horizon conventions, the independence test's disagreement is about duration rather than about an informational edge over 28 analysts and 71% institutional ownership, and the specific link this dive is priced on carries no disclosed revenue share at all.
bull: Real, dated demand growth sits on the chain's money corner. Q2 2026 Power Generation sub-application sales grew 29% year over year ($3,098M vs $2,407M, filing_evidence[7]), power generation RETAIL sales specifically grew 72% (mapping placement evidence, Utility Dive 2026-08-11, part of the sibling onsite-reciprocating-gensets placement this dive treats as context), and the disclosed segment sentence attributes it directly to the mechanism this dive is priced on: 'Power Generation – Sales increased in large reciprocating engines and in turbines and turbine-related services, primarily in data center applications' (filing_evidence[2]). The comparable disclosed elsewhere on this chain, Johnson Matthey's $360 million acquisition of Cormetech, is guided to more than GBP200 million in combined sales at mid-teens operating margins by 2026/27 (WebSearch 2026-09-06, hydrocarbonprocessing.com/matthey.com), the closest disclosed proxy for what aftertreatment content itself can earn.

The mechanical earnings-quality battery is broadly clean despite a real, disclosed tariff shock. Beneish M-score -2.405 (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs, well inside the -1.78 review threshold), Altman Z 5.07 (SAFE, 8 of 8 inputs), accruals of -3.07% of average assets (net income $8,882M against operating cash flow $11,739M, average assets $93,174.5M), inside the 5% caution band and in the conservative direction, and cash conversion of 132.17% (operating cash flow over net income). All four Piotroski misses (d_roa, d_leverage, gross_margin, asset_turnover) trace to the SAME externally disclosed, quantified cause, the FY2025 tariff hit, not to manipulation, and CAT is already showing real pass-through: Q2 2026 GAAP operating margin (20.9%, filing_evidence[1]) already exceeds FY2024's pre-tariff full-year peak (20.17%) even with a larger tariff bill guided for 2026.

Some of the market's most aggressive positioning has already partially unwound rather than compounded further, and not by chasing the print: the 2026-06-30 high of 1,064.90 was hit BEFORE the Q2 2026 release, and today's 813.94 is 23.57% below it. A name that beat by this much (adjusted EPS $8.17 versus roughly $6.20 consensus, WebSearch 2026-09-06, biggo.com/manufacturingdive.com) and still trades below both its own pre-print level (830.03) and its pre-print-quarter high is not obviously euphoric on this print alone, whatever the trailing-twelve-month picture.
bear: The trailing multiple has done virtually all of the work over the past year, not earnings, on the only annual EPS figures this dive can verify without inventing a number. Using the last annual EPS on disk at each point in time: at the 2025-09-09 52-week low (418.09), the trailing P/E on FY2024 EPS ($22.5738, net income $10,788M over 477.9M shares) was about 18.52x; at the 2026-06-30 52-week high (1,064.90), the trailing P/E on FY2025 EPS ($19.0888, net income $8,882M over 465.3M shares, itself DOWN 15.44% year over year on the tariff hit) was about 55.79x; today (813.94) it is about 42.64x. The stock is up 94.68% from the low while the most recent annually reported earnings figure available to price it against actually FELL. This is not a clean TOO_LATE decomposition (data_gaps: no quarterly net income is on disk to build a true trailing-twelve-month figure, and the two quarterly EPS points that ARE on disk, $4.62 in Q2 2025 and $7.77 in Q2 2026, show real acceleration a pure annual comparison misses), but it is real, sourced, and the single largest reason this dive will not call INVESTABLE at this price.

The specific exposure this dive is priced on has no disclosed revenue attribution anywhere on disk. Aftertreatment content is a sub-component of the Power Generation sales line, itself roughly 37.6% of the Power & Energy segment's Q2 2026 sales ($3,098M of $8,238M), itself roughly 40.1% of total company sales ($8,238M of $20,543M), inside a $67,589M FY2025 revenue base; no filing on disk breaks out the aftertreatment share of even that innermost line. Cummins carries an ACTIVE placement on this identical link this same run (duplicate_exposure), competing for the same qualification-locked mechanism rather than diversifying it, and CAT itself is not an undiscovered name by any measure this run could find: 28 sell-side analysts carry it with a consensus Buy rating and a 975.61 average target, and institutions hold 71% of the float (WebSearch 2026-09-06). The chain's UNDISCOVERED tag (crowdedness 28) describes the narrow narrative angle, not the stock, and this dive treats that distinction as real but thin: there is no informational edge in owning one of the Dow's most followed names for a reason nobody has quantified.

The 2026 tariff bill is guided larger than 2025's (approximately $2.6 billion versus $1.3-1.5 billion, WebSearch 2026-09-06, wfaa.com), and a real, disclosed, litigation-linked item is already inside the very quarter the bull case leans on for margin recovery: 'Operating profit in the second quarter of 2026 included $392 million of expected International Emergency Economic Power Act (IEEPA) tariff recoveries' (filing_evidence[4]), about 9.1% of the quarter's $4,295M consolidated operating profit, described as 'expected' rather than settled. Strip it out and Q2 2026 GAAP margin is roughly 19.0% (3,903/20,543), still above Q2 2025's 17.3% but a smaller recovery than the headline 20.9%, and independence_test.falsification names the litigation reversal that would make this a live risk rather than a footnote.

rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 total revenue growth landing within or above the guided mid-to-high-teens range, and Power Generation sub-application growth staying at or above 30% (watch_triggers[1]), both observable at the Q3 2026 release expected in late October 2026 (inside this dive's review window).

rows.why: 19% sits between FY2025's tariff-compressed 16.5% and FY2024's pre-tariff peak of 20.17% (both VERIFIED, SEC XBRL companyfacts), near the top of the FY2018-2025 range (10.91% to 20.17%). Q2 2026's GAAP margin (20.9%, filing_evidence[1]) already exceeds the FY2024 peak despite a larger guided 2026 tariff bill ($2.6B versus FY2025's $1.3-1.5B, WebSearch), which argues price realization ($595 million this quarter alone, per the 8-K) is outrunning the tariff drag faster than the FY2025 annual print alone suggests; 19% assumes that race continues but does not fully repeat Q2's pace (which was partly aided by the $392 million IEEPA item, filing_evidence[4]).
rows.structural_reason: A mix shift toward higher-margin Power Generation and aftertreatment content (qualification-locked per the chain's own capture score of 65) plus CAT's own demonstrated history of passing tariff costs through to price with a lag, both argue for margin recovery above the FY2025 trough over a 5-year path.
rows.leading_indicator: Full-year or sustained quarterly GAAP operating margin holding above 18% (watch_triggers[0]) once the $392 million IEEPA item is excluded or confirmed recurring, observable at the Q3 2026 and Q4 2026 releases.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a reinvestment return separately from the headline FCF CAGR, and no company-disclosed ROIC figure appears in the fetched 8-K.
rows.why: A rough return on invested capital, computed here (not disclosed) as NOPAT (operating income at an assumed 22% tax rate) over long-term debt plus equity, runs 14.82% (FY2022), 23.00% (FY2023), 21.77% (FY2024) and 16.72% (FY2025), the last of which is the tariff-depressed trough. 18% assumes partial recovery toward the FY2023-2024 range but not all the way, given the larger guided 2026 tariff bill and the fact that this formula's invested-capital denominator includes debt raised partly for buybacks rather than only for operating capacity, an acknowledged caveat (data_gaps).
rows.structural_reason: The same tariff pass-through and Power Generation mix-shift argument as the operating_margin row; not independently repeated here.
rows.leading_indicator: Full-year 2026 operating margin and capex efficiency trending back toward the FY2023-2024 range rather than settling at the FY2025 trough, observable at year-end.

rows.why: No disagreement. 2.5% perpetual growth sits at or below the long-run nominal GDP ceiling this desk's own base rates cite, and is the one input this dive would not change for a scale industrial machinery and engine maker with real but cyclical pricing power, short of an unregulated monopoly.

rows.note: This dive builds a hand-derived FCF-equivalent CAGR of 12.12% from the three rows above (9% revenue CAGR compounding revenue to $104.03B by year 5, times a 19% steady-state margin, times the FY2025 cash-conversion ratio [FCF/operating income 0.7998] held flat), rather than comparing revenue_cagr_5y directly to the market's FCF-CAGR solve, which sibling dives in this corpus found to be a category mismatch. Against the market's 28.57% five-year implied ask, that is a 16.45-point gap, larger than this file's own 12.34-point horizon_spread, so on the DEFAULT five-year convention this reads as a real gap per method section 7, not a horizon-convention artifact. But at the ten-year convention the same market ask falls to 16.23%, only 4.11 points above this dive's 12.12% base case and INSIDE the 12.34-point horizon_spread: per method section 7, a gap smaller than horizon_spread is not a gap. Even this dive's own STRETCH case (12% revenue CAGR, 21% margin, 17.54% FCF-equivalent CAGR) leaves a 10.93-point gap at 5 years but nothing near the 10-year ask. The direction (market implies more) is genuine and survives the tougher convention; whether it survives the friendlier one is a real, named, unresolved disagreement about DURATION rather than about direction, echoing the very first dive in this corpus (VRT, 2026-08-29), where an apparent gap on the 5-year convention was found to be mostly a convention artifact once the 10-year reading was checked. This dive does not resolve that disagreement in either direction; it names it and prices the would_buy_zone on the tougher convention rather than the one that makes the entry case look better.

expectations_gap.gap_vs_spread: Method section 7: a gap smaller than horizon_spread must say which of the two it is claiming, and a gap inside the band is not a gap. The 5-year convention gap (16.45pp) exceeds the file's 12.34pp horizon_spread and survives; the 10-year convention gap (4.11pp) does not survive, sitting inside the band. Unlike VRT, where the 10-year convention closed MOST of the gap and the dive still landed WATCH rather than reverting to the draft's TOO_LATE, this dive's 10-year reading closes essentially ALL of the claimed gap, which argues the disagreement here is even more purely about duration than VRT's was.
expectations_gap.denominator: 5 of 5 required rows populated. Market-implied column, counted honestly: 1 of 4 numeric drivers SOLVED and category-matched (terminal, where this dive states no disagreement); 3 of 4 NULL in the filed solve (revenue_cagr_5y, operating_margin, reinvestment_return are not decomposed). net_gap_direction is therefore built from a hand-derived FCF-equivalent estimate, not a single clean market-implied number, and is checked against BOTH the 5-year and 10-year conventions, per the standing lesson from VRT's dive: enumerate every convention on both sides before claiming a gap, then vary them rather than merely declaring them.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market's current price (813.94, down 23.57% from the 1,064.90 high hit 2026-06-30 but still up 94.68% from the 418.09 low of 2025-09-09) embeds a reverse-DCF-implied five-year free-cash-flow CAGR of 28.57%, more than double this dive's own defended base case (approximately 12.12%, built from a 9% revenue CAGR and a 19% steady-state operating margin, itself already near the 88th percentile of CAT's own FY2018-2025 margin range), while the trailing annual EPS actually available at each point in time moved the other way: EPS computed off the last-reported fiscal year fell 15.44%, from $22.5738 (FY2024) to $19.0888 (FY2025), even as the stock's trailing P/E on that same denominator rose from about 18.52x at the 52-week low to a peak near 55.79x at the 52-week high and about 42.64x today.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: This reads as extrapolation of one narrow, real but recent segment surge (Power Generation sub-application sales +29% in Q2 2026, retail sales +72%, both inside the Power & Energy segment that is itself roughly 40% of total company sales) onto the whole $67.6 billion diversified machinery and engine business, at exactly the moment a full-year tariff shock ($1.3-1.5 billion in 2025, guided to widen to about $2.6 billion in 2026, WebSearch) had just cut FY2025 consolidated operating margin from 20.2% to 16.5% and depressed the trailing EPS the market's current multiple is being paid against. CAT is also one of the most heavily analyzed, most institutionally owned names this desk has evaluated (28 sell-side analysts, 71% institutional ownership, WebSearch 2026-09-06), so if a mispricing exists here it is about DURATION (how many years the data-center surge compounds before it normalizes toward CAT's cyclical historical growth rate) rather than about undiscovered information: 27 other analysts have the same 8-K this dive does.
independence_test.falsification: By the Q3 2026 release (expected in late October 2026, based on CAT's own cadence: Q3 2025 was reported 2025-10-29, WebSearch), if Power Generation sub-application sales growth has stayed at or above roughly 50% year over year AND consolidated GAAP operating margin has held at or above the 20.9% Q2 2026 level net of the $392 million IEEPA tariff-recovery item already disclosed this quarter (i.e., the margin improvement is not solely that one 'expected' item), this dive's caution about extrapolating one segment and one quarter is wrong, and the market's higher forward FCF path is closer to being earned than this dive's own defended 12.12% base case allows.

earnings_quality.basis: Grade B: a mechanically clean earnings-quality battery carrying real, disclosed, quantified headwinds with a coherent single explanation, not a clean A and not a Beneish-breach C. Clean: Beneish M-score -2.405 (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs, well inside the -1.78 review threshold); Altman Z 5.07 (SAFE, 8 of 8 inputs); accruals of -3.07% of average assets (net income $8,882M against operating cash flow $11,739M, average total assets $93,174.5M FY2024-FY2025), well inside the 5% caution band and in the conservative direction (cash exceeds earnings); cash conversion 132.17% (operating cash flow over net income, matching the O1 profile's canonical field). Piotroski 5 of 9 (MIDDLING, 9 of 9 inputs found), missing d_roa, d_leverage, gross_margin and asset_turnover; all four trace to the SAME externally disclosed, quantified cause, the FY2025 tariff hit ($1.3-1.5 billion, WebSearch): ROA fell from 12.31% to 9.53%, gross margin fell from 37.97% to 33.79%, leverage (total liabilities / total assets) rose from 77.79% to 78.38%, and asset turnover fell from 73.97% to 72.55%, a coherent, externally-caused pattern rather than four independent or manipulation-shaped misses. DSO drifted up from 50.67 days (FY2023) to 52.28 (FY2024) to 58.97 (FY2025), a real but modest +16.3% two-year rise with no filed explanation found this run, named as a mild, unexplained caution rather than folded into the tariff story. Capex-to-depreciation rose from 0.745x (FY2023) to 0.923x (FY2024) to 1.247x (FY2025), the healthy direction (rising reinvestment ahead of demand, consistent with the disclosed restart of the 10-MW genset platform on the sibling placement), not a flag. One further mild, disclosed item: $392 million of Q2 2026's $4,295 million operating profit (about 9.1%) is an 'expected' IEEPA tariff recovery (filing_evidence[4]), a real, quantified, litigation-linked item rather than an unexplained recurring 'one-time' item of the kind that defines grade C; excluding it, Q2 2026 GAAP margin is still roughly 19.0% (3,903/20,543), still an improvement over Q2 2025's 17.3%. One mild governance flag: a planned CFO succession (Andrew Bonfield retiring 2026-10-01, Kyle Epley, a nearly-30-year CAT veteran, effective 2026-05-01), orderly and internally sourced per this run's WebSearch, not filing-verified this run. No auditor change: PricewaterhouseCoopers has served since 1925 and was ratified again for fiscal 2026 (WebSearch). No related-party dealings or SEC investigation/restatement found (WebSearch, not exhaustive). Not A because of the DSO drift, the IEEPA item's 'expected' (unsettled) framing, and the CFO-succession flag; not C because none of the accrual, Beneish, or capex-to-depreciation tests breach C-grade territory, and the Piotroski misses are coherently explained by one disclosed external cause rather than by unexplained or recurring items. The grade does not itself cap this dive's verdict: WATCH is reached independently on the size and duration-sensitivity of the expectations gap, the lack of any disclosed link-specific revenue, the duplicate exposure with Cummins, and the stock's extreme trailing-multiple expansion (bear[0]-[3]), which this dive treats separately from the mechanical earnings-quality battery.

would_buy_zone.basis: Forward-solving the same growing-FCF-plus-Gordon-terminal-value formula behind quality.reverse_dcf (base_fcf $8,918.0M, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year explicit horizon; this reconstruction reproduces the filed enterprise value almost exactly at g=28.57%: $396,290.7M against the filed $396,339.325M, a 0.01% difference, confirming the formula is faithful before it is used to solve forward) for two FCF-CAGR-equivalent growth paths built from this dive's own expectations_gap assumptions rather than the market's 28.57% ask: low uses a conservative like-for-like build (7% five-year revenue CAGR, 17% steady-state operating margin, FY2025's cash-conversion ratio held flat), which is a 7.64% FCF-equivalent CAGR and $324.65 a share; high uses a stretch build (12% revenue CAGR, 21% margin, near CAT's own pre-tariff FY2024 peak), which is a 17.54% FCF-equivalent CAGR and $509.94 a share, both above this dive's own base case (9%/19%, 12.12% FCF-equivalent, $400.91). Each is computed by inverting the same formula for enterprise value at each g, then converting EV to price with the same canonical net debt ($23,983.0M) and FY2025 share count (465,300,000) the filed solve already uses. Both bounds sit inside 0.3x-2.0x of the 813.94 last close and strictly below price_ref.value.

would_buy_stress: Re-running the identical forward solve at the 10-year explicit horizon instead of 5-year, holding base_fcf, the discount rate and the two growth paths fixed, raises the same growth-consistent band to $394.12 (conservative) to $887.90 (stretch): $887.90 is already ABOVE today's price. This is the same convention-sensitivity method section 7 flags directly: on the tougher 5-year convention the market's ask (28.57%) is far outside even this dive's stretch case (17.54%), a real, wide gap (10.93pp); on the friendlier 10-year convention the market's own headline number falls to 16.23%, only 4.11 percentage points above this dive's 12.12% base case and well inside the file's own 12.34pp horizon_spread, meaning the gap this dive claims on the default convention would not read as a gap at all on the other one. The would_buy_zone above is deliberately drawn on the tougher 5-year convention rather than the one that makes the entry case look better, per the discipline VRT's original dive established in this corpus. See expectations_gap.rows[net_gap_direction] for the same finding stated as a table row.
data_gaps: No revenue percentage is disclosed or sourced anywhere on disk tying the aftertreatment/catalyst content specifically to CAT's financials; it is a sub-component of the Power Generation sales line, itself part of the Power & Energy segment, itself part of a $67,589M company (bear[1]).

No sales-by-segment dollar breakout (only profit by segment) appears in the fetched 8-K for Construction Industries or Resource Industries, so the exact share of total company sales that is genuinely data-center-driven cannot be sized more precisely than the Power Generation sub-application line already used throughout this dive.

Quarterly net income is not on disk (data/market/CAT.json fundamentals carries only FY totals plus the two EPS figures quoted from the fetched 8-K), so a true trailing-twelve-month EPS and P/E cannot be computed without inventing a number the venue rule forbids. The FY2024-vs-FY2025 fixed-denominator comparison used throughout this dive (bear[0], independence_test, valuation_snapshot) is the most defensible substitute on the data available, but it understates the H1 2026 earnings acceleration already visible in the two quoted quarterly EPS figures ($4.62 to $7.77, +68.2%).

The $72.1 billion order backlog, $9.4 billion new-orders, mid-to-high-teens FY2026 revenue guide, and $2.6 billion 2026 tariff guide figures used throughout this dive (watch_triggers, expectations_gap, earnings_quality) are WebSearch-only and NOT present in the fetched 8-K text on disk. Every one is tagged INFERRED.

No pcs block exists at all for CAT in data/market/CAT.json (neither axis A nor axis B); this dive's crowdedness read rests entirely on this run's WebSearch rather than the repo's own crowdedness store.

notes.text: This dive's central, load-bearing finding is the trailing-multiple math in bear[0] and independence_test, built entirely from VERIFIED SEC XBRL figures already on disk (FY2024/FY2025 net income and share counts) crossed against the price series: the stock is up 94.68% over twelve months while the last annually reported EPS figure available at each point FELL 15.44%. This is the closest thing to a clean multiple-expansion-vs-earnings decomposition this analyst's log has produced to date (per data/stocks/_dive-log.json's own shadow-book note: six straight prior dives found CONTRACTING, not expanding, multiples, which is why none of them could sustain a TOO_LATE call). This dive does not call TOO_LATE anyway, because the decomposition is incomplete (quarterly net income is not on disk, data_gaps) and the two quarterly EPS points that ARE on disk show real, recent acceleration a pure annual comparison misses. If a future re-run can source quarterly net income (or a TTM EPS figure) via a data request, this is the single highest-value number to add to this file: it would let a re-run either confirm the multiple-expansion read or retire it.

The would_buy_zone is drawn on the tougher 5-year reverse-DCF convention, per the ESLT/VRT precedent, deliberately not on the 10-year convention that would draw a much friendlier (higher, closer-to-spot) zone; see would_buy_stress for the 10-year figures.
